questions.question_text: INS Mahendragiri, a Project 17A (Nilgiri-class) stealth frigate commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 11 July 2026, was built by which shipyard?

2. It became India's 45th World Heritage Site.
3. It is the first World Heritage Site in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill, 2025, passed by the Assam Legislative Assembly on 27 November 2025:
1. It applies uniformly to Sixth Schedule areas and to the State's tribal communities.
2. Entering a second marriage while concealing an existing one is punishable with up to 10 years' imprisonment.
3. Repeat offenders face double the punishment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Bill passed on 27 November 2025 punishes a second marriage without dissolving the first with up to 7 years, and up to 10 years if the earlier marriage is concealed; repeat offenders get double the punishment, and clerics who solemnise such marriages can be fined. It does not apply to Sixth Schedule areas or to the State's tribal communities.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 1 is wrong: Sixth Schedule areas and tribal communities are excluded.

fact_checks.claim: Assam Assembly passed Prohibition of Polygamy Bill on 27 Nov 2025: up to 10 years for concealing a marriage, 7 years otherwise, double for repeat offenders; not applicable to Sixth Schedule areas and tribal communities

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: At its board meeting of 19 June 2026, SEBI approved 'GARUDA'. What is it?

options.text: A new route for open-market buybacks through stock exchanges
A framework for intraday borrowing by mutual funds
A green-channel mechanism to speed up the launch of schemes by Alternative Investment Funds
A quick process for transmission of small-value securities claims

solution.explanation: GARUDA stands for 'Green-Channel: AIF Rollout Upon Document Acknowledgement'. It lets AIFs begin fund-raising for Non-Accredited Investor schemes within 10 working days of filing their placement memorandum, instead of 30 days. The same meeting also approved MF intraday borrowing, stock-exchange buybacks and Quick Transmission Processing.
steps: GARUDA: Green-Channel: AIF Rollout Upon Document Acknowledgement
solution.why_others_wrong: Intraday borrowing, exchange buybacks and Quick Transmission Processing were separate decisions of the same meeting.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A green-channel mechanism to speed up the launch of schemes by Alternative Investment Funds

fact_checks.claim: SEBI board meeting 19 June 2026: GARUDA = Green-Channel: AIF Rollout Upon Document Acknowledgement, to speed AIF scheme launches; also MF intraday borrowing, exchange buybacks, QTP

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 in July 2026. What does it extend the 1971 Act's protection to?

solution.concept: Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026
solution.explanation: The amendment extends to the National Song the protection that the 1971 Act gives the National Anthem: insulting Vande Mataram or obstructing its singing becomes punishable with imprisonment of up to three years, a fine, or both. The Rajya Sabha passed it on 29 July and the Lok Sabha on 30 July 2026; assent was on 6 August 2026.
steps: Act amended: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
Penalty: up to 3 years, fine, or both
solution.why_others_wrong: The bill concerns the National Song, not the Emblem, Calendar or Pledge.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The National Song, Vande Mataram

fact_checks.claim: Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026: extends similar protection to the National Song; up to three years; assent 6 August 2026

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026:
1. It amends Section 13 of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
2. Registration of a birth or death delayed beyond two years needs an order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
3. Registration delayed by more than one year but less than two years needs an order of a Sessions Judge.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Delayed registration of births and deaths
solution.explanation: Act No. 12 of 2026 amends Section 13 of the 1969 Act. A registration delayed by one to two years needs an order of the District Magistrate, Sub-Divisional Magistrate or an Executive Magistrate authorised by the DM; one delayed beyond two years needs an order of a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class, after verification and payment of the fee. Assent was given on 6 August 2026.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 3 is wrong: one-to-two-year delays need an executive magistrate's order (DM, SDM or authorised Executive Magistrate), not a Sessions Judge.

fact_checks.claim: Act No. 12 of 2026 amends Section 13 of the RBD Act, 1969; one to two years: DM/SDM/authorised Executive Magistrate; beyond two years: Judicial Magistrate of the First Class
Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026; assent 6 August 2026

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026:
1. States and Union Territories must designate Special Fast Track Courts for offences under it.
2. Investigations are generally to be completed within six months.
3. Trials are to be held day-to-day and concluded within three months of the chargesheet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The amendment (assent 31 July 2026) raises jail terms and fines, provides for Special Task Forces, requires States and UTs to designate Special Fast Track Courts, sets a general two-month limit for investigations, and requires day-to-day trials concluded within three months of the chargesheet.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: investigations are generally due within two months, not six.

fact_checks.claim: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026; assent 31 July 2026; Special Fast Track Courts; investigation generally within two months; trials within three months of chargesheet

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the decisions of the SEBI board meeting held on 19 June 2026:
1. The meeting was chaired by Madhabi Puri Buch.
2. Open-market buybacks through the stock exchange route were reintroduced with effect from 1 August 2026.
3. Quick Transmission Processing covers claims of up to ₹10,000 for physical securities and ₹30,000 for demat securities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The 214th board meeting, chaired by Tuhin Kanta Pandey, reintroduced open-market buybacks through exchanges from 1 August 2026 (to be completed within 66 working days), created Quick Transmission Processing for small claims (₹10,000 physical, ₹30,000 demat), allowed MF intraday borrowing and approved the GARUDA green channel for AIFs.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 1 is wrong: the meeting was chaired by SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey.

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the changes to the Press Note 3 (2020) FDI rules approved by the Union Cabinet on 10 March 2026:
1. Investments with up to 10% non-controlling beneficial ownership from entities of land-border countries are permitted under the automatic route.
2. Proposals in specified manufacturing sectors get a 90-day approval timeline.
3. Majority ownership and control of the investee company must remain with resident Indian citizens or Indian-owned entities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Press Note 3 of April 2020 required government approval for any FDI from countries sharing a land border with India. On 10 March 2026 the Cabinet allowed up to 10% non-controlling beneficial ownership through the automatic route (with reporting to DPIIT) and a 60-day approval window for specified manufacturing sectors such as capital goods, electronic components and polysilicon, with majority ownership and control staying with resident Indians.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement 2 is wrong: the fast-track approval timeline is 60 days.

fact_checks.claim: Cabinet press release dated 10.03.2026: up to 10% non-controlling beneficial ownership from land-border countries under automatic route; 60-day timeline for specified manufacturing sectors

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953 as the first state of independent India created on a linguistic basis, was carved out of which state, and what was its capital?

solution.explanation: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 from the Telugu-speaking districts of Madras State, with Kurnool as its capital. It was the first state in independent India formed for linguistic reasons; it merged with the Telugu areas of Hyderabad State in 1956 to form Andhra Pradesh.
solution.why_others_wrong: It was carved from Madras State, and its capital was Kurnool, not Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam or Guntur.

fact_checks.claim: Andhra State formed 1 October 1953 from Madras State; capital Kurnool; first state formed in independent India for linguistic reason

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Haryana was formed on 1 November 1966 under which law?

solution.explanation: Haryana was carved out of Punjab on 1 November 1966 under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. It shares its capital, Chandigarh, with Punjab.
solution.why_others_wrong: The 1956 Act reorganised states on linguistic lines, the 1960 Act split Bombay State and the 1971 Act created north-eastern states.

fact_checks.claim: Haryana formed on 1 November 1966 after the Punjab Reorganisation Act was passed; shares capital Chandigarh with Punjab
